subject.title: feat(gateway): add context engine control API

question: Should OpenClaw core own a generic context-engine control API now, and should it be HTTP-only or also a first-class Gateway RPC method surface?
rationale: The PR introduces new core Gateway routes, operator scopes, and public context-engine plugin contract methods; those are durable product/API choices that automation cannot safely accept without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor core API after repair
options.body: Accept the direction, require the security/discovery fixes, docs/SDK alignment, and a fresh rebase before merge.

options.title: Keep it HTTP-only and hidden
options.body: Allow the direct HTTP endpoints but mark the contextEngine.* descriptors non-advertised or move scope sentinels away from the client method catalog.

options.title: Pause or close direction
options.body: Decline the core API for now and ask downstream control planes to use a plugin-specific or ClawHub integration until a maintainer sponsors the generic contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core API after repair
recommendation.body: Accept the direction, require the security/discovery fixes, docs/SDK alignment, and a fresh rebase before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Most likely product/API decision route from recent context-engine/session work and Gateway client API documentation activity.
